sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A rhizomatous perennial native to North America, with upright stems 1–3 m tall. Lower leaves are often opposite and upper leaves alternate.

sections.title: Flowers and tubers
sections.text: The yellow flower heads resemble small sunflowers. The edible tubers are swollen ends of rhizomes, so they are underground stems rather than roots; they contain abundant inulin.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The tubers are eaten raw or cooked. Unlike common sunflower (H. annuus), grown chiefly for its seeds, this species is mainly harvested for its tubers.
